prompt: Before Voltmarkt's April 2025 analysis, run three checks on the orders placed that month (the UTC days of order_ts) and their order lines, and return one row for each check. order_id is unique: the orders checked, and how many rows are copies of an order_id already counted. every order has a line: the orders checked, and how many of them have no order line. every line has a known product: the order lines of those orders, and how many of them name a product_id that products does not hold. A line with a missing product_id names no product_id, so it counts as checked but not as failing. In every check, checked_rows and failing_rows count rows: an order_id that appears twice in orders counts twice, and each of its order lines also counts twice, once for each copy. Return three columns, in this order: check_name (the text order_id is unique, every order has a line or every line has a known product), checked_rows and failing_rows. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, write the uniqueness check: the rows against the distinct order_id values.
Keep the orders step at one row per order, with no join to its lines, or every order with two lines looks like a copy.
why_this_works: Each check counts the rows it looked at and the rows that break its rule, at the grain the check names.
